file_rules.why: A renamed column (currency -> fare_currency) shifts every downstream mapping; safer to reject the whole file than silently misroute all rows.

rules.why: Nothing to settle or trace without them.
BSP PNR format; lowercase or wrong length cannot be matched to GDS.
IATA airline codes are always 2 letters; 3-letter codes (e.g. AIR) are not valid IATA.
Unknown airline code cannot be settled; no contract on file.
Booking class is a single character; lowercase (k) is a data-entry error.
Class not in airline's published inventory cannot be priced.
Missing hyphen (BOMDXB) or wrong length cannot be parsed into origin/destination.
A ticket from and to the same airport (BOM-BOM) is not a valid itinerary.
Unknown airport code (XYZ) cannot be routed or settled.
Extra decimals (4520.555) indicate a calculation error; cannot round without losing audit trail.
Negative fare amount (refund/void) belongs in a separate adjustment file, not a ticket-issue file.
Unknown currency (INX) cannot be converted or settled.
BSP ticket number must be exactly 13 digits plus separator; wrong length (098-75716779) cannot be matched.
Prefix/airline mismatch (125- with AI) means the ticket was issued on a different carrier's stock.
Non-ISO format (25/11/2026) cannot be reliably parsed across locales.
A ticket issued after the file date is impossible; indicates a date error.
Late tickets are valid but need manual settlement review; flag rather than reject to preserve revenue.
IATA agency codes are always 8 numeric digits; wrong format cannot be looked up in BSP agency register.
Same ticket appearing twice in one file is a system duplicate; count it but do not write it twice.
